confidence_notes: I used three web searches. One found the latest RBA AUD/USD rate: 0.6720 USD per AUD at 4.00 pm on 18 November 2026, shown on the RBA exchange-rates page. That figure came through the search summary, not from reading the page directly. The other two searches looked for Tottori food and drink prices. They found crowdsourced Tottori figures from citycost.org: an inexpensive meal at about JPY 1,694 (about USD 10), a mid-range dinner for two at about JPY 5,588 (about USD 34) and a cappuccino at about JPY 575 (about USD 3.5). The site's table layout made it unclear which column belonged to which city. My inexpensive-meal anchor of USD 7.50 is deliberately lower than that USD 10 figure. Tottori ranks among Japan's cheapest cities, and set meals, ramen and teishoku there usually cost about JPY 900-1,300. The beer and coffee anchors also reflect national prices. For beer, travelcostcalculator.org gave about USD 3.92 per draught in Tottori, one sushi bar listed JPY 600, and Expatica's June 2026 Numbeo figures for Tokyo gave JPY 550. I found no reliable Tottori wine price, and the only cocktail figure was an unverified USD 8.96 for signature cocktails in lounges. So I estimated both from how they usually compare with beer in regional Japan: highballs and standard cocktails at about JPY 700-900, and house wine at about JPY 600-700. Accommodation prices were not searched, as instructed. They are model estimates from general knowledge. Tottori has very few hostels, so the dorm and private-room anchors are the least certain. The hotel anchors assume the low-cost business hotels near Tottori Station. Prices may be higher in peak summer around the sand dunes and during Obon.
comparable_city_reasoning: I treated Tottori as a small regional Japanese city with low prices, similar to Matsue, Yonago and other San'in or Shikoku prefectural capitals. Its restaurant and drink prices should be at or below Japan's national averages and clearly below Tokyo and Osaka. Accommodation is mostly business hotels near the station, with few hostels.
